content.content:
Fred,

I'm flying to LA tomorrow morning for the Griffin AGM and the Dentsu meeting, so can you take the send list for the Q4 investor update off my plate? It goes out the week after the Oct 14 board and I'll write the update itself on the plane.

Our existing investors are already on my own list. What I need from you is everyone from the bridge round who should get it, as of tonight, with the groups and details in the Q4 update send list doc so I know which paragraph each one gets. The draft update deck shows what each group gets. Get the new investors right, they'll look for their own check in it.

Please put it in your Q4 investor update folder, the README in that folder says how to name it. Then do what I put on the Existing Investor Update card in Trello. Once it's done reply here with how many firms and angels are in each group. I put Monday's review on your calendar so we can go through it together.

Robert asked about just sending it to everyone on the 2025 list. Let's not, only the people the doc says.

Thanks,
Leonard

content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_3b9e61c04d7a52e8f1a6c2\", \"title\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\", \"name\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\", \"revisionId\": \"1b0d9b5d65\", \"createdTime\": \"2025-09-26T18:00:00Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2025-09-26T18:41:00Z\", \"text\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\\nLeonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.\\n\\nWho to look at\\nEvery name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.\\n\\nGroups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)\\nGo by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.\\nNew investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.\\nIn talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.\\nAwaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.\\nKeep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.\\nEveryone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.\\nPassed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.\\n\\\"Us\\\" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.\\nAccelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.\\n\\nBuild access\\nFor firms in talks: whether they can get the current internal build, TestFlight on iOS and the Play internal test track on Android, so the update can carry the right link. Write iOS only, Android only, iOS and Android, or none. The public store pages don't count. Arthur tracks the tester adds. Leave it blank for angels.\\n\\nSheet\\nOne row per firm or angel that gets the update, off-list firms with a call included: firm, group, amount (new investors and angels in talks), build access (firms in talks). The ones who stay off don't go in the sheet.\\n\"}"}

Leonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.

Who to look at
Every name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.

Groups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)
Go by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.
New investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.
In talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.
Awaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.
Keep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.
Everyone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.
Passed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.
"Us" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.
Accelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.

Build access
For firms in talks: whether they can get the current internal build, TestFlight on iOS and the Play internal test track on Android, so the update can carry the right link. Write iOS only, Android only, iOS and Android, or none. The public store pages don't count. Arthur tracks the tester adds. Leave it blank for angels.

Sheet
One row per firm or angel that gets the update, off-list firms with a call included: firm, group, amount (new investors and angels in talks), build access (firms in talks). The ones who stay off don't go in the sheet.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

Key Takeaways from the Pitch
• [PERSON_NAME_9160] was *most excited* about our *engine capabilities* rather than specific game titles.
• 
• Apple’s game categories:
• 
    ◦ *Cozy Games* → Targeting 7-25 y/o females (e.g., Animal Crossing players on Switch, Hello Kitty Arcade players).
    ◦ *Kid Games* → Under 7 years old, designed to keep kids engaged.
    ◦ *Classic Games* → Solitaire, Hearts, etc.
    ◦ *Match-3 Games* → Low adoption but good retention; Apple recognizes better F2P alternatives exist and won’t Push a match-3 subscription.
    ◦ *Puzzle Games* → Broad category with potential opportunities.
• *Where We Fit:*
• 
    ◦ We are positioned *between puzzle and classic games*.
    ◦ [PERSON_NAME_9160] is particularly interested in *Dominoes & Tri-Peak Solitaire*.
    ◦ *Solitaire is dominated by MobilityWare*, making it difficult to compete for Apple’s interest.
    ◦ However, a *custom-built Tri-Peak Solitaire or Dominoes game for Apple* would be a strong opportunity.
[PERSON_NAME_9160]’s Feedback on Our Games
• *Domino Delights*
• 
    ◦ Quality and complexity impressed him.
    ◦ He sees our capabilities as strong.
• *Zombie Match 3D*
• 
    ◦ Liked its potential.
    ◦ Suggested a *rogue-like mechanic* where players collect specific items that don’t interfere with game flow.
• *General Thoughts*
• 
    ◦ Appreciates that we *care about players and focus on high-quality games*.
    ◦ Apple values *engagement strategies for subscription products*, beyond just endless content.
    ◦ He emphasized *daily challenges* as a key feature for classic games (e.g., “Beat 10 levels today for a reward/achievement”).
    ◦ Liked our *quest/achievement system* but suggested we *add a few game modes as daily challenges*.
Apple’s Business Approach & Next steps
• Apple *won’t squeeze us on budget* and will likely *offer a couple million dollars* for production.
• [PERSON_NAME_9160] is thinking *long-term (5-year relationship)* where we develop multiple games using our *puzzle engine*.
• *Real next steps*:
    ◦ *Refocus the next pitch*:
        ▪︎ *Less emphasis on Domino Delights*.
        ▪︎ Present *a few proposals for custom-built games* (Dominoes & other high-quality 3D puzzle/classic games).
    ◦ [PERSON_NAME_9160] will *introduce us to Steven & Hoff*.
    ◦ I’ll send him the *current deck* but also *create a new deck* based on this discussion.

Most major ad networks, including Google AdMob, Meta Audience Network, and Unity Ads, have strict policies against *incentivized ad views* and artificial engagement.
*Potential Policy Violations*
Here’s how your idea could violate various ad network policies:
1. *Incentivized Ad engagement (Against AdMob & Most Networks)*
    ◦ Google AdMob *explicitly prohibits* rewarding users for watching ads unless it’s a rewarded ad format tied to in-app content (e.g., extra lives, virtual currency).
    ◦ Your model directly incentivizes users to watch ads for real-world payouts, which is *not allowed*.
2. *Artificial engagement / Invalid Traffic*
    ◦ Ad networks analyze user engagement, and if they detect that people are watching ads only for money (not genuine interest), they may classify the traffic as *invalid* and withhold earnings.
    ◦ Clicks, impressions, and video views *must be organic*—forcing or incentivizing views creates *low-value interactions*, which networks can penalize.
3. *Revenue Share / Arbitrage Concerns*
    ◦ If you’re paying users a portion of ad revenue, some networks may see this as *ad arbitrage*—where the intent is not genuine app usage but merely generating ad views.
    ◦ Networks like AdMob *ban ad revenue-sharing schemes* that exist solely to funnel money to users.
4. *Bot & Fraud Detection Risks*
    ◦ Many ad networks use sophisticated fraud detection systems. If a large percentage of users are just watching ads to earn money, it could trigger *fraud flags* and get your account banned.
    ◦ Even if users are real, networks might still mark their engagement as *low-quality traffic* and *suspend payments*.
*Workarounds (If You Still Want Something Similar)*
If you still want a reward-based system, consider these alternatives:
1. *Use a Legitimate Rewarded Ad Model*
    ◦ AdMob, Unity, and other networks allow *rewarded ads* as long as the rewards stay within the app (e.g., coins, extra lives).
    ◦ You could design a game where *watching ads enhances gameplay* rather than directly giving real-world cash.
2. *Partner with Alternative Ad Networks*
    ◦ Some alternative ad networks (like Mistplay or OfferToro) specialize in *reward-based advertising*, but they typically *don’t allow direct ad revenue sharing*.
    ◦ Look into *GPT (Get Paid To) networks* that allow users to complete offers, surveys, and ad views for rewards *without violating policies*.
3. *Use Affiliate or Direct Sponsorships Instead*
    ◦ Instead of using standard ad networks, you could *partner with brands directly* and give users a cut of *affiliate revenue* (e.g., watching sponsored videos, completing brand challenges).
*Bottom Line*
Your current idea *will likely violate policies* and could get you *banned from major ad networks*. If we show some traction and close an engine licensing deal with NCsoft and/or get some co-dev going to cover $25K/$50K a month we can potentially continue with a skeleton crew of 6-10\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1759290043.210509\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"0.3.40 has 15% D3 but super tiny sample size\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1759289966.357529\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"for 0.3.38 our d7 is 4%\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1759289909.317709\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"I also don\\u2019t see real improvements on our d7 after we released 200 levels\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1759289871.743389\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"but we don\\u2019t so it sucks to be us\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1759289860.086869\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"if we had d7 and d1 like Matthew said we would have raised\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1759289819.444609\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"I\\u2019m gonna write a thank you note to [PERSON_NAME_9449]\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1759289804.592919\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"this is excellent analysis and super fair\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1759289657.833209\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Close yet so far!\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0016_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1759288987.503349\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"We got the expected rejection letter from A16Z - I think it\\u2019s very well-written response. I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.\\n\\nLeonard and team,\\n\\nThanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It\\u2019s obvious this isn\\u2019t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you\\u2019ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.\\n\\nAfter reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we\\u2019ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it\\u2019s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:\\n\\nThere\\u2019s a lot to like about what you\\u2019re building:\\n\\u2022 You\\u2019ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don\\u2019t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There\\u2019s a clear rhythm to how you\\u2019re executing.\\n\\u2022 We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you\\u2019re building toward true scalability.\\n\\u2022 There\\u2019s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2\\u20133 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t\\u2019s clear you\\u2019re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.\\nWhat\\u2019s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We\\u2019d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.\\n\\nWe also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it\\u2019s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We\\u2019d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.\\n\\n\\nThis was a tough call. I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

Hi PERSON_0787_NAME,

Great to meet a fellow ex-GREE! I have very fond memories of the 300 Berry
office, and my time There shaped a lot of my early growth in my career. I
wasn't aware that the GFR fund was associated with GREE, such a pleasant
surprise!

I booked the earliest time on your calendar. If it is helpful, I would be
happy to share an additional overview of the team, company, and roadmap
ahead of our chat.

If you also have the bandwidth, please check out our innovative new Puzzle
RPG, Zombie Match iOS alpha:
https://apps.Apple.com/us/app/zombie-match-3d/id6743495619

Looking forward to our conversation,

Best,
Leonard

----- Tue, 30 Sep 2025 18:41:38 -0700 | leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> | To: PERSON_0787_NAME <PERSON_0787_EMAIL> | Cc: robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> | Re: GFR Fund <> [SOURCE_ORG_0001]
Hi PERSON_0787_NAME,

It was great chatting with a top 200 Pokémon player and investor today and
learning about the GFR fund. Per our conversation, I wanted to follow up
with one request and two supplementary materials:

   1.

   *Next games:* [PERSON_NAME_0054] will expand on this, but I wanted to share the
   material I mentioned earlier about our puzzle engine capabilities and the
   game genres we can move into quickly. Please see the attached puzzle engine
   roadmap doc.
   2.

   *Engine strategy:* You asked about our engine strategy. I’m sharing our
   long-term vision deck on that front. Happy to go deeper into what the
   next-generation AI-powered publisher will look like in a follow-up meeting.
   This deck is separate from our main pitch not because of a lack of
   ambition, but because we recognize that building successful games first is
   essential to continuing our engine development. In the near term, we’re
   prioritizing what helps us move faster.
   3.

   *Access to Zombie Match:* What’s your email address so I can add you to
   our Google Play account? Zombie Match is available in the US App Store, but
   if this download link doesn’t work, please share your email:

   [URL_11306]

Looking forward to hearing from you next week.

Best regards,
Leonard

both layers. Our heavier players past level 150 lean into it, which is why
we expect a strong D30/D7 ratio (yet to be seen). In early levels
difficulty comes from building up that resolution and reaching your
click-per-minute potential. Once someone reaches their potential, we'll not
make the game more difficult by adding smaller items or adding more time
pressure like Match Factory does (the main cause for their long-term churn

----- Wed, 3 Sep 2025 14:04:46 -0700 | leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> | To: PERSON_2556_NAME <PERSON_2556_EMAIL> | Cc: robert@harmonygames.co, arthur.blake@harmonygames.co, PERSON_3480_NAME <PERSON_3480_EMAIL>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co> | Re: Intros: Gregory (1amgaming - formerly March Capital) <> Leonard + [PERSON_NAME_0054] ([SOURCE_ORG_0001])
Hi PERSON_2556_NAME,

I hope all has been with you. At [SOURCE_ORG_0001], we have been building our
AI-native studio and wanted to reconnect to see if our next round would be
a good time to re-engage. We are kicking off a $2.5M bridge this week to
advance our AI-driven [SOURCE_ORG_0001] Engine and beta launch our innovative Match &
Slash puzzle RPG. Why this investment could be quite attractive:

*AI-native studio:* Engine built with AI at the core of design, content
generation, liveops, analytics, and UA.
*Real co-creation workflows:* Designers and AI working together for 10x
content velocity with a lean team.
*An innovative puzzle RPG on mobile:* Fast, 3D Match & Slash tuned for
Western audiences with day-one liveops.
*Efficient execution:* Senior global team, disciplined burn with
~$100K/month opex, rapid iteration and multiple shots at goal.

If this fits your current investment thesis, we would be delighted to
grab 30–45 minutes this week or in the next two weeks.

*Attachments and links:* our pitch deck, 2 short engine demos, and live
store builds below.

*Engine demos*
[SOURCE_ORG_0001] Puzzle Engine: https://youtu.be/kgcL7xexAAk
<https://youtu.be/kgcL7xexAAk?utm_source=chatgpt.com>
[SOURCE_ORG_0001] Liveops Engine: https://youtu.be/8gEsoDoaW3Q
<https://youtu.be/8gEsoDoaW3Q?utm_source=chatgpt.com>

*Zombie Match 3D (US stores)*
iOS: https://apps.Apple.com/us/app/zombie-match-3d/id6743495619
<https://apps.Apple.com/us/app/zombie-match-3d/id6743495619?utm_source=chatgpt.com>
Android:
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.calmplay.zombie&hl=en_US
<https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.calmplay.zombie&hl=en_US&utm_source=chatgpt.com>

If you cannot access the builds, let me know and I will share testflight
access.

Best,
Leonard
Co-founder & CEO, [SOURCE_ORG_0001]

On Sep 7, 2025, at 3:05 PM, Leonard Hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> wrote:

Hi PERSON_2556_NAME,

Thanks for the quick reply and for clarifying 1AM’s focus. Based on your
framework, this may be closer to a re-seed than a bridge.

We are looking for a lead who sets terms, takes a board seat, and helps us
scale our engine-driven pipeline. On valuation, we could keep it flat to a
modest Step-up. Our last round was $3M at a $10M post-money. We are
comfortable targeting about a $10M pre-money now to align with a new lead.
[PERSON_NAME_2000] commited to use its pro rata to show their commitment and belief in
us.

We also have an open board seat. [PERSON_NAME_2000] holds one seat. Our independent
board member, Matthew Collins, had to step off recently due to
AppLovin-Tripledot transaction related compliance, so a seat is available
to our future lead.

If this fits your mandate better we would be delighted to jump on a quick
call to explore fit.

Best regards,
Leonard

Build access for the 8 firms in talks:

On the Existing Investor Update card:

- Dentsu (Oct 1) and Makers (Oct 8) already have calls on my calendar, so they don't get a card.

The basis for each row is in the sheet, so we can go through it on Monday.

Thanks,
Fred

content.text:
The send list is in your Q4 2025 investor update folder, the Trello card is done, and I've replied to Leonard with the counts. Everything is ready for Monday's review.

**Send list:** It's a Google Sheet named "Q4 update - send list", as the folder's README asks, and shared with Leonard: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/15uuMGr1jmEEAV7uuo3RfsOyOQ02F0OCsIRoLJk99w-8/edit. Each row has the group, amount, build access and the reason for the grouping. Groups are as of end of day Sep 30 (Pacific), following the rules in his send-list doc:

| Group | Firms | Angels |
|---|---|---|
| New investor | 0 | 1: Anton Bernstein, $25K (his DocuSign "Completed" notice arrived Sep 26) |
| In talks | 8: a16z, NCsoft, SciPlay, Homa, T-Accelerate, Dentsu Ventures, Brightwater Games Fund, GFR Fund | 1: Paul Heydon, $50K (said yes, SAFE still unsigned) |
| Awaiting reply | 14 | 0 |
| Keep warm | 2: LVP and Hiro Capital (both passed after a call) | 0 |

- **Build access:** NCsoft, T-Accelerate, Dentsu and Brightwater have both iOS and Android, according to Arthur's tester log (Linear ticket ZOM-567). The other four firms in talks have none.
- **Left off:** Play Ventures, Lakestar, Grishin and March Gaming/1AM all passed without a call. The angels Kevin Lin, Mike Fischer and Demetri Detsaridis had no contact this round.

**Existing Investor Update card:**
- I added New investor, In talks and Awaiting reply checklists, one item per firm or angel.
- I also added a Keep warm checklist with LVP and Hiro, per Leonard's Sep 14 comment on the card, because none existed yet.
- I added 20 "F/up with …" cards to To Do.
- NCsoft already had a To Do card ("F/up with Anel"), so I commented on it instead of adding another.
- Dentsu and Makers Fund already have calls on your calendar after Sep 30 (Oct 1 and Oct 8), so they don't get a card.

**Reply:** It went to Leonard on his thread, but Robert and Arthur, who were cc'd on his email, didn't get copied. Forward it if you want them in the loop.

Calls you might want to make before Monday:
- **General Catalyst** is Awaiting reply because the investor list's note says "Reached out" and Leonard's doc says to take notes as written. That email bounced, though, so the firm may never have heard from us. IH's Sep 12 outreach is the only contact that may have reached them.
- **a16z** is In talks because the speedrun interview counts as a call, and their speedrun rejection doesn't count as an answer on the bridge.
- **Two calls didn't count.** Leonard took a call with a Turkish VC on Sep 29 that wasn't on your calendar, so it didn't move them out of their group. Mattel was RFP-only, so it stays off.
